voiceover: Same six products. Same twenty-five years. Same Bureau of Labor Statistics data. <break time="500ms"/> Under median wages — four out of six got cheaper. Under CPI — three got more expensive. Under the minimum wage — five out of six. Under gold — everything's a bargain. <break time="1000ms"/> Shrinkflation is real. Your chip bag lost twenty-three percent of its weight. Your coffee can lost more than a third. But the biggest shrinkage isn't in the package. <break time="1000ms"/>

visual.description: Split-screen summary — 4 grouped bar charts in a 2×2 grid. Each chart shows the number of products above/below 1.0 for one deflator. Top-left: 'Median Wage' — 2 red bars (above), 4 green bars (below). Top-right: 'CPI' — 3 red, 3 green. Bottom-left: 'Minimum Wage' — 5 red, 1 green. Bottom-right: 'Gold' — 0 red, 6 green. Each bar chart animates in sequence (10-frame stagger between charts). The bars use Muted Red (#E06070) for above-1.0 and Muted Green (#5BBF8C) for below. Product names labeled on each bar. Common title: 'Same Data. Different Ruler.' in Montserrat Bold 36px. Source: 'BLS, FRED, DOL, LBMA' in Sage Silver, bottom.

notes: THE VISUAL SUMMARY. This 2×2 grid should be the clearest, most information-dense frame in the video. Each mini-chart is simple: bars going up (red) or down (green) from a baseline. The progression from top-left (2 red) to bottom-left (5 red) visually tells the story of shifting perspectives. Stagger the 4 charts: top-left first, top-right second, bottom-left third (the punch), bottom-right last (the absurdity). 6-frame stagger for bars within each chart, 10-frame stagger between charts. Dot grid background active. The 1000ms break at the end creates space before the final scene.
